Fact.Name: Has a farming business reported on Schedule F
Fact.Description:
Whether the return reports a farming business on Schedule F (Form 1040), Profit or Loss From Farming. The gate for this whole module.
A return with no farm leaves this unanswered, which resolves Complete false through /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome and makes line 9 a Complete $0. This is an intake question about the RETURN, not a printed Schedule F line: the paper form has no "do you farm?" box, because filing the schedule at all is the answer.
SCOPE NOTE the form itself prints, recorded rather than modelled: Schedule F is NOT filed for income from agricultural services if that is the filer's principal source of income, from breeding or caring for pet animals, from managing a farm for a fee, or for sales of livestock held for draft, breeding, sport or dairy purposes. The first three go to Schedule C and the last to Form 4797.

Fact.Name: Schedule F box C: the accrual accounting method is elected (filer entry)

The instructions say "If you use the accrual method, check the box for" Accrual and then complete Part I line 9, Part II and Part III - so accrual is the elected, stated case and cash is the ordinary one. That makes an unanswered box safest as CASH, which is exactly what /scheduleFUsesAccrualMethod does with it.

Fact.Name: Schedule F line 3b: taxable amount of cooperative distributions
Fact.Description:

WHY THE UNANSWERED ARM IS NOT $0 WHEN PAYER DOCUMENTS EXIST: if it were, a patron could record every Form 1099-PATR they received and this line would still print blank, so the distributions the payer reported to the IRS would reach neither line 9 nor gross farm income. The default is the FULL line 3a figure because that is what the instructions make taxable in the ordinary case: the only distributions a farmer excludes are "patronage dividends from buying personal or family items, capital assets, or depreciable assets", which the instruction says to "Enter these amounts on line 3a only".
THE SPLIT IS STILL THE FILER'S JUDGEMENT AND IS NOT COMPUTED. Whenever the filer answers the intake, their number wins outright and is not capped, floored or cross checked against line 3a - the engine has no cross fact Limit, and a silent cap would replace a judgement the filer is entitled to make. The default only fills the blank a recorded payer document would otherwise leave.
DIRECTION: taxpayer ADVERSE for a patron who records the documents and never answers this line, since they are taxed on distributions they might have been entitled to exclude - the correct direction, since the alternative would omit income the payer reported to the IRS - and it is visible rather than silent, because the printed line carries the figure. No committed scenario carries a /form1099Patrs item, so nothing moves.

Fact.Name: Schedule F line 6a covers Form 1099-MISC box 9 proceeds
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe consistency fence for Schedule F line 6a. When the return has a complete line 6a entry and the Form 1099-MISC collection is complete, the entered gross proceeds must be at least the sum of all complete-safe box 9 crop-insurance amounts. The document total is a reporting floor, not a second addend: the filer still reports the aggregate on Schedule F and the box 9 values are never added to line 9 independently. If either side is unanswered, this fence stays TRUE so the pre-existing complete-safe line 6b behavior is preserved; a positive reported box 9 with no line 6a entry is named as the remaining intake handoff rather than silently retyped.
FOR A RETURN THAT CLAIMS SCHEDULE F FARM INCOME, A FIRST CASE RUNS AHEAD OF THE FLOOR TEST: when /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome is TRUE, the Form 1099-MISC collection is complete, its box 9 total is above zero and /writableScheduleFLine6aCropInsuranceReceived is NOT answered, this fence is FALSE and line 6b is Incomplete. What the arm enforces is the missing GROSS entry: box 9 is an amount the payer reports as received this year and the recipient instructions route to Schedule F, so a farm return that leaves line 6a blank against that document has not entered a figure its own documents prove exists. The arm makes NO claim about the taxable amount - line 6b is the filer's own figure, and a line 6c election lawfully makes it smaller than line 6a - and it adds box 9 nowhere; it only holds line 6b Incomplete until line 6a is entered. On a return where this arm does not fire, the fence stays TRUE on a blank line 6a and line 6b resolves to the bare-line $0 default that every unanswered dollar line on this schedule carries; that default is not created by this fence. NOT covered here, deliberately: (1) a filer with a positive box 9 who has NOT claimed Schedule F is not refused by this fence, because the arm is gated on /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome; that return is refused instead by form1099Misc:/knockoutForm1099MiscCropInsuranceWithoutScheduleF unless the filer attests the document as reported correctly; (2) prefill of line 6a from the document total is the application's; (3) a return that files BOTH a Schedule F and a Form 4835 whose box 9 belongs to the rental (Form 4835 line 5a) is refused unless the amount is also entered on line 6a, because no fact links a Form 1099-MISC to one activity - the successor is the per-document selector already named for Schedule C.

Fact.Name: Schedule F line 6b: taxable amount of crop insurance proceeds received in 2025
Fact.Description:

When 6a and 6b are both answered and contradict 6c, this fact resolves INCOMPLETE rather than accepting either value - a return whose own entries disagree about how much crop insurance is taxable this year is not computable, not silently favourable to one direction over the other.
A BLANK LINE 6b IS $0 ONLY WHERE $0 IS AN ANSWER THE RETURN SUPPORTS. In most cases crop insurance proceeds are reported in the year received, so a positive line 6a with a blank line 6b and no line 6c deferral election is the same self-contradiction, and it now resolves INCOMPLETE instead of silently entering $0 of taxable proceeds - the $0 carried the whole of line 6a out of line 9, /scheduleFGrossIncome and /totalIncome. The blank still gives $0 on the three shapes that support it: line 6a unanswered, a line 6a that is not above $0, and a line 6c election, which by the all-or-nothing rule defers every eligible dollar of that farm's proceeds to 2026 and leaves nothing taxable this year.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture reported on Schedule F (line 8)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "How much of your Form 4797 line 35 recapture comes from property whose section 179 deduction or depreciation you took on Schedule F?" HELP TEXT: "When business use of section 179 property or listed property drops to 50% or less, Form 4797 Part IV figures a recapture amount on line 35. Report it as other income on the schedule on which you took the deduction. Enter the farm's part here and leave it out of your line 8 other income answer: it is added to line 8 for you. If the property was used both in farming and to produce income, enter only the part attributable to the farm; that part is subject to self-employment tax. Increase your basis in the property by the recapture amount." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 12, right column; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sf.pdf, page 5, left column). ASKED WHEN: /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome is true and form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureToRoute is above zero. UNANSWERED: $0; when the amounts entered on every schedule do not add up to line 35, the return does not complete (form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture). VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0. WHAT IT FEEDS: /scheduleFForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocated, hence line 8 (/scheduleFLine8), line 9, net farm profit, Schedule SE and the qualified business income computation, and the Form 4797 allocation check.

The Schedule F term of form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureAllocatedTotal, and what /scheduleFForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg carries to line 8, so the check and the line read one quantity; an amount allocated on a return that files no Schedule F counts $0 and the allocation check refuses the return rather than losing it.

The complete-safe default survives untouched for every filer who discloses none of the three, which is the overwhelming majority.

Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Schedule F line 33: total farm expenses
Fact.Description:
Schedule F Part II line 33, "Total expenses. Add lines 10 through 32f", rounded to whole dollars. THIRTY summands, in printed order: 10 through 22 down the left column, then 23 through 32f down the right.
"IF LINE 32f IS NEGATIVE, SEE INSTRUCTIONS" - read, costed, and found to need NO BRANCH, the same shape as the Part III footnote finding on /scheduleFLine49. The instruction it points at says: "If line 32f is a negative amount, subtract it from the total of lines 10 through 32e. Enter the result on line 33." That is a rule about PARENTHESES, not about arithmetic. The filer who capitalizes preproductive period expenses under section 263A is told to enter them "in parentheses on line 32f (to indicate a negative amount)" - a MAGNITUDE with a paper convention for its sign - and the instruction then tells that filer which way to take the magnitude. This module stores line 32f SIGNED (that is what a Dollar with no Min 0 fence is), so the printed mainline "Add lines 10 through 32f" already produces total(10..32e) + (-capitalized) = total(10..32e) - capitalized, which is the number the instruction describes. Adding a branch would double the negation.
ROUNDED HERE, because line 33 is a printed line and the paper carries it in whole dollars, exactly as /scheduleFGrossIncome rounds line 9. Line 34 is then the difference of two whole-dollar figures and needs no rounding of its own.
NOT GATED on /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome, deliberately: it is a printed intermediate like lines 1c, 44, 47, 49 and 50, all of which are ungated. The gate sits once, at /scheduleFPreAtRiskNetProfitOrLoss, so a return that answers an expense but never claims a farm cannot manufacture a farm loss. Complete for any subset of answered legs.
SECTION 464: when the 50% prepaid farm supplies limit binds, the disallowed excess is already netted OUT of /scheduleFLine28 (and, if line 28 alone cannot absorb it, /scheduleFLine26 and then /scheduleFLine16 - see /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed for the waterfall), before this Add ever runs. This total therefore literally equals the sum of the printed lines 10 through 32f, deducted figures throughout, and needs no separate downstream adjustment: /scheduleFPreAtRiskNetProfitOrLoss subtracts THIS fact from line 9 unchanged. /scheduleFLine33BeforePrepaidLimit is the same THIRTY-leg sum computed from the PRE-waterfall line 16/26/28 figures instead - it exists only to give the section 464 test its own denominator without depending on its own output, and is not itself printed anywhere.
A THIRTY-FIRST ADDEND, NOT ONE OF THE PRINTED THIRTY: /scheduleFAtRiskLossFromPriorTaxYear (the section 465(a)(2) carry-in), $0 for every filer with no prior-year disallowed at-risk loss. See the section 465(a)(2) banner comment above this fact's own definition for why it belongs here rather than in a 32a-32f slot or as a downstream adjustment to line 34.

See /scheduleFLine33 for the printed total and /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed for the waterfall.
ALSO CARRIES the section 465(a)(2) at-risk carry-in addend (/scheduleFAtRiskLossFromPriorTaxYear), the same THIRTY-FIRST addend /scheduleFLine33 carries, and for the same reason Pub. 225 gives for the section 464 denominator itself: "other deductible farm expenses" is "all Schedule F deductions ... except prepaid farm supplies" - the carry-in is a genuine Schedule F deduction (IRC 465(a)(2), the Instructions' own Lines 32a Through 32f placement), so it belongs in the 50% test's denominator exactly as depreciation and every other non-prepaid expense already does. A return with BOTH a section 464 trigger and a nonzero carry-in therefore sees a LARGER denominator (and so a larger 50% limit, and a SMALLER or zero section 464 disallowance) than the same return without the carry-in - the correct direction, not a double-count: the carry-in only ever shrinks or moots a limitation that is separately about prepaid supplies, it never manufactures one.

Help text: prepaid farm supplies are supplies paid for during the year but not used or consumed during it; see Instructions for Schedule F, Prepaid farm supplies, and Pub. 225 chapter 4, Prepaid Farm Supplies. Unanswered posture: defaults to $0 (no prepaid supplies), complete safe - the normal case for a farm that did not prepay. Validation: Dollar, Min 0. NOT MODELLED: the line 16 three-condition prepaid-FEED test (purchase-not-deposit, business purpose, no material distortion of income) that decides whether prepaid feed is deductible in the year paid at all - a filer determination with no modelled inputs, exactly like the poultry special rules and the binding-commitment facts-and-circumstances test. This intake only feeds the 50% CEILING on what the filer has already decided is deductible.
NO UPPER BOUND ON THE INTAKE: /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesInputsConsistent does not refuse a prepaid total larger than lines 16 + 17 + 26 + 28 as attested - that total is a lawful intake. WHETHER THE RETURN FILES is separate: if the filer enters a total above those four lines and the section 464 limit disallows anything, /knockoutScheduleFPrepaidTotalAboveItsFourLines refuses the return, because the limit itself may then be understated. NAMED GAP: the Instructions' definition of prepaid farm supplies also includes POULTRY, and poultry sits on none of lines 16, 17, 26 and 28, so a filer whose prepayment is poultry has nowhere on this screen to report it and may instead answer $0 - a silent omission, stated here because it is the worse direction than a refusal. Widening the question's wording waits on the poultry-placement decision (Part I line 1b against Part II), because the question cannot ask for a number without saying which line it belongs to, and the printed guidance contradicts itself on that.

Fact.Description: Asked when the return claims Schedule F farm income (/claimsScheduleFFarmIncome). This dictionary cannot yet compute where that cost belongs or how much of the 50% test it occupies, so answering Yes stops this return here rather than place the amount on the wrong line, omit it from the 50% test, or guess at a placement the instructions do not settle. Fact.Name: Knockout: a section 464 disallowance figured from a prepaid total larger than the four lines it is asked about
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the section 464 limit disallows part of the prepaid farm supplies (/scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed above $0) AND the prepaid total the filer entered (/scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesTotal) is larger than the sum of lines 16, 17, 26 and 28 before the limit - the four lines the prepaid question asks about. WHY. The 50% limit is measured against the farm's OTHER deductible farming expenses, which /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesOtherExpenses figures as line 33 before the limit less the whole prepaid total. That subtraction is right only when every prepaid dollar sits inside line 33. A prepaid total above the four lines means at least part of it does not sit on them: it may sit on another line 33 line (then the subtraction is right), or on no line at all, such as a poultry cost deducted nowhere this year (then the subtraction removes dollars that were never in line 33, the limit is too small and too much is disallowed). The return cannot tell which, so it refuses rather than file a disallowance that may be too large. Every return whose prepaid total fits inside the four lines, and every return where the limit disallows nothing, is unaffected. SCREEN: "The prepaid farm supplies you entered are more than the feed, fertilizer and lime, seed and plants, and supplies expenses on lines 16, 17, 26 and 28, and part of your prepaid supplies deduction is limited this year. This product cannot yet tell which of your other expenses the rest belongs to, and that decides how much is limited, so this return cannot be filed here." COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: each operand's completeness is tested first and an All short-circuits on a Complete-false operand.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a qualified joint venture farm whose split needs a per-spouse input this return does not ask
Fact.Description: Blocks submission on a qualified joint venture farm (/scheduleFIsQualifiedJointVenture) in either of two populations where dividing the combined farm by the spouses' respective interests is not the same as each spouse's own Schedule F: (1) THE AT-RISK LIMIT APPLIES TO A LOSS (/scheduleFAtRiskLimitationApplies true and /scheduleFPreAtRiskNetProfitOrLoss below $0). The limit is each taxpayer's own amount at risk, but /writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk is one amount for the whole farm, so the loss is capped before the split and divided by interest, where each spouse's own cap could allow a different loss to each (a 50/50 farm with a $20,000 loss and $1,000 and $7,000 at risk splits -4,000 / -4,000 here against -1,000 / -7,000). (2) CONSERVATION RESERVE PROGRAM PAYMENTS on Schedule SE line 1b (scheduleSE:/scheduleSeLine1bConservationReservePaymentsAtLeastZero above $0). The line 1b exclusion turns on whether the spouse was receiving social security retirement or disability benefits, and scheduleSE:/writableScheduleSeLine1bReceivingSocialSecurityBenefits is one answer for both spouses, so a joint venture where only one spouse was receiving them is divided as though both were, or neither. SCREEN: "You elected to treat your farm as a qualified joint venture, and part of the farm's result depends on something that can differ between you and your spouse (the amount each of you has at risk in the farm, or whether each of you was receiving social security benefits when the Conservation Reserve Program payments arrived). This product asks those questions once for the whole farm, so this return cannot be filed here." A qualified joint venture with neither is unaffected, and so is every farm that is not a qualified joint venture. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: the joint venture gate and the at-risk gate are unconditionally Complete, and each dollar operand is read after its own completeness test.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: the filer (or spouse) has more than one farming business
Fact.Description: ASK: "Do you, or your spouse if filing jointly, operate more than one farming business that is reported on its own Schedule F?" HELP: answer Yes if you have two separate farms (for example, one run by each spouse, or two businesses kept on separate books). A qualified joint venture you and your spouse elected is ONE farm for this question. ASKED WHEN: the return claims Schedule F farm income (/claimsScheduleFFarmIncome). UNANSWERED: read as No. VALIDATION: Boolean. FEEDS /knockoutScheduleFMoreThanOneFarm: this return carries exactly one Schedule F, so a Yes refuses rather than combine two farms into one, which puts the whole of both on one owner's Schedule SE and applies one at-risk amount and one section 464 test across two businesses.

Fact.Name: Knockout: more than one farming business (this return carries one Schedule F)
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the return claims Schedule F farm income and the filer answers Yes to /writableScheduleFMoreThanOneFarm. SCREEN: "This product can prepare only one Schedule F. Because you have more than one farming business, each needing its own Schedule F, this return cannot be filed here." Complete-safe: unanswered or No is unaffected, the same posture as /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome on a return with no farm.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: the farm's prior-year unallowed passive activity loss carried into 2025
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Does this farm have a passive activity loss that was not allowed in earlier years (from your 2024 Form 8582) and carried forward to 2025? Enter the amount." HELP TEXT: a farm you did not materially participate in during an earlier year may carry an unallowed passive loss. ASKED WHEN: the return claims Schedule F farm income. UNANSWERED POSTURE: $0. VALIDATION: not less than zero. WHAT IT FEEDS: /knockoutScheduleFPassiveFarmNotPooled (a carry-in is refused: the farm is not in the Form 8582 pool).

Fact.Name: Knockout: a farm the filer did not materially participate in, with a loss or beside a suspended passive loss
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the return claims Schedule F farm income, the filer answered No on box E (did not materially participate in the farm), and either line 34 is a loss or this return's passive activity pool suspends a loss that the farm's profit could absorb. WHY. A farm the filer does not materially participate in is a passive activity. Its loss is allowed only against passive income, figured on Form 8582, and its profit is passive income that frees other passive losses. This dictionary's Form 8582 pool (scheduleE) holds the rentals and the Schedule K-1s but not the farm: line 34 reaches Schedule 1 line 6 in full. So a passive farm loss would be deducted in full against wages, and a passive farm profit would leave the other passive losses suspended. The return is refused instead. NOT REFUSED: box E unanswered or Yes; a passive farm with a profit on a return whose pool suspends nothing (its profit changes no passive allowance, and line 34 is right as it stands). Also refused: a farm that carries its own prior-year unallowed passive loss (/writableScheduleFPriorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss above $0), whatever box E says, because that loss can be allowed only through the Form 8582 pool.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: other deductible farm expenses for the section 464 test
Fact.Description: The section 464(d) denominator: total expenses BEFORE the section 464 waterfall (/scheduleFLine33BeforePrepaidLimit, NOT the printed /scheduleFLine33 - using the printed total here would be circular, since it now depends on this fact's own downstream disallowance through the reduced feeder lines) MINUS the prepaid farm supplies total, floored at $0. "Other deductible farm expenses" excludes the prepaid supplies themselves by definition - the instruction's worked example subtracts them out before taking 50%.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 464 50% prepaid farm supplies limit
Fact.Description: 50% of /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesOtherExpenses, rounded to whole dollars - the most the filer can deduct this year for prepaid farm supplies when the limit applies.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: the section 464 50% prepaid farm supplies limit applies (filer entry)
Fact.Description: Asked when /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesTotal exceeds /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesLimit (the 50% test would otherwise bind). Question: "Does the 50% limit on prepaid farm supplies apply to you?" Help text: it does NOT apply if you are a farm-related taxpayer (your main home is on a farm, your principal business is farming, or a family member meets either test) and either (a) your prepaid farm supplies expense is more than 50% of your other deductible farm expenses because of a change in business operations caused by unusual circumstances, or (b) your total prepaid farm supplies expense for the preceding 3 tax years is less than 50% of your total other deductible farm expenses for those 3 years - see Pub. 225 chapter 4, Prepaid Farm Supplies, Exceptions. Answer Yes if the limit applies to you (neither exception fits); answer No if you qualify for either exception. TRUE means the limit applies. Unanswered posture: MOOT (resolves FALSE) when the mechanical 50% trigger has not fired - the question is never asked and no deduction is at stake. When the trigger HAS fired (cash method, prepaid total exceeds the 50% limit) and this question is unanswered, /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesLimitApplies (the complete-safe reading) resolves INCOMPLETE rather than silently granting the exception - a filer cannot receive a full, statute-uncapped deduction on an unverified claim that the two IRC 464(d)(2) exceptions apply. Validation: Boolean, no default answer offered.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 464 limit applies (complete safe)
Fact.Description:
NOT a plain complete-safe default: unanswered does NOT always resolve FALSE. Three cases. (1) MOOT: a filer not on the cash method resolves FALSE regardless of whether the question was asked. A cash filer is gated on /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesInputsConsistent (which resolves INCOMPLETE only on a NEGATIVE prepaid total - a prepaid total above the four reducible lines is a lawful intake, not an inconsistent one, since the definition of prepaid farm supplies reaches poultry, which sits on none of them; whether such a return FILES is a separate question /knockoutScheduleFPrepaidTotalAboveItsFourLines decides once the limit disallows anything); inside that gate, a prepaid total at or below the 50% ceiling resolves FALSE, because no deduction is at stake and the question is never even shown. (2) the writable is COMPLETE: the filer's own answer, from one of two sources (below). (3) the trigger HAS fired and neither source is complete: this Case's Then reads the writable directly, unguarded by IsComplete, so this fact - and everything downstream (/scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed, the section 464 waterfall, /scheduleFLine33, line 34) - resolves INCOMPLETE rather than picking FALSE (full deduction) or TRUE (limit applies) on a live, statute-capped amount the return has not confirmed. A complete-safe default is for MOOT questions, never for a present, capped amount.
TWO SOURCES FOR THE EXCEPTION ANSWER. When the filer has started the detailed IRC 464(d)(2) evidence review (/scheduleFPrepaidDetailedEvidenceStarted, true as soon as ANY of the eight new inputs is answered), the answer comes from /scheduleFPrepaidReviewedLimitApplies - the computed farm-related-taxpayer test reconciled against the legacy attestation, Incomplete when the two contradict and Incomplete on a qualified joint venture, whose two spouses cannot share one history. A return that has answered none of the eight keeps the legacy attestation as case (3)'s source.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 464 prepaid farm supplies excess disallowed this year
Fact.Description:
The prepaid farm supplies excess disallowed for 2025 under section 464(d): when the filer uses the cash method AND has confirmed the limit applies AND the prepaid total exceeds the 50% limit, the LESSER of the statutory excess (prepaid total minus the limit) and the sum of the four reducible printed legs (lines 16, 17, 26 and 28 before the limit, each floored at $0), so the waterfall can never remove more than those legs hold; otherwise $0. The body is Switch(Case When IsComplete(/scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesLimitApplies) Then (limit applies ? capped excess : $0)) with NO total fallback, so an UNRESOLVED limit decision cannot fall through to a silent $0 disallowance.
APPLIED AT THE SOURCE, not downstream, across a FOUR-LINE WATERFALL (28 -> 26 -> 16 -> 17): this fact is netted directly against /scheduleFLine28BeforePrepaidLimit (the FIRST leg - "supplies" is the closest name-match to "prepaid farm supplies" of the feeder lines), overflowing to /scheduleFLine26BeforePrepaidLimit via /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowedAfterLine28, then to /scheduleFLine16BeforePrepaidLimit via /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowedAfterLine26, and finally to line 17 via /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowedAfterLine16 and /scheduleFLine17 (that fourth leg's own netting lives on those two facts, not here) - so the printed /scheduleFLine33 (which sums the printed, already-netted /scheduleFLine16, /scheduleFLine17, /scheduleFLine26 and /scheduleFLine28) equals the sum of its own printed components whenever the limit binds, and /scheduleFPreAtRiskNetProfitOrLoss can subtract the printed line 33 unchanged. No IRS instruction names which of the four lines carries the reduction or in what order; this waterfall order and the cap on the four legs are both modelling choices, not a reading of the statute.
THE FULL STATUTORY EXCESS IS NOT CAPPED: /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesCarryForward computes the whole excess (prepaid total minus the 50% limit, floored at $0) independently of this fact's four-leg cap, because what the statute defers to a later year is the whole excess, not only the part of it that happened to fit on lines 16, 17, 26 and 28. The two agree on every return whose prepaid total is within those four legs, which is every return that does not prepay poultry.
THE RESIDUE WHERE THE PREPAID TOTAL EXCEEDS THE FOUR LEGS is why /knockoutScheduleFPrepaidTotalAboveItsFourLines refuses the return whenever this fact is above $0: the part of the excess above the four legs is disallowed by the statute and would not be taken off any printed line if the return filed. Two cases show why the knockout cannot tell which applies and so refuses both alike: (i) if that part was deducted on some OTHER expense line the waterfall does not reach, letting the return file would leave the filer KEEPING a deduction the statute defers - an over-deduction, UNDER-TAX in the taxpayer's favour; (ii) if it was deducted nowhere on the return - the poultry-bought-for-resale-and-not-resold case - there would be no tax effect at all, and the amount would simply be disclosed on /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesCarryForward for the year it is used. Witness: scheduleF/s917-prepaid-total-exceeds-expense-basis pins the refusal for case (ii); s917-prepaid-negative-total-refuses, s917-prepaid-partial-detail-cannot-fallback and s917-prepaid-qjv-detailed-history-refuses pin the unresolved-limit guard (which leaves the limit fact unresolved only on a NEGATIVE prepaid total).
NOT MODELLED: no carry-FORWARD is applied automatically to a later return; the current-year excess is visible on /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesCarryForward for a future unit to consume - the same shape as /writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk's undisclosed section 465(a)(2) carryforward gap this dictionary also does not close end-to-end.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 464 disallowed excess still unabsorbed after line 28
Fact.Description: /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed minus /scheduleFLine28BeforePrepaidLimit, floored at $0 - the portion of the disallowed excess line 28 alone could not absorb, carried to /scheduleFLine26 (the waterfall's second leg) at /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed. Not itself printed; see /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed for why the waterfall exists.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 464 disallowed excess still unabsorbed after lines 28 and 26
Fact.Description: /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowedAfterLine28 minus /scheduleFLine26BeforePrepaidLimit, floored at $0 - the portion of the disallowed excess neither line 28 nor line 26 could absorb, carried to /scheduleFLine16 (the waterfall's third and last leg). Not itself printed; see /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed for why the waterfall exists.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 464 prepaid farm supplies excess carried to a later year (not consumed)
Fact.Description: The whole excess this year's return could not deduct under the 50% limit - prepaid farm supplies total minus the 50% limit, floored at $0 - which Pub. 225 chapter 4 states is deductible "in the year you use or consume the supplies" (the following year, for supplies other than poultry). This fact computes that excess directly rather than reading /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed, because that fact is capped at the four reducible printed legs so the waterfall cannot remove more than they hold, while what the statute defers to a later year is the whole excess, not only the part of it that happened to fit on lines 16, 17, 26 and 28. The two agree on every return whose prepaid total is within those four legs, which is every return that does not prepay poultry; where they differ, the difference is exactly the residue named on /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed - see /knockoutScheduleFPrepaidTotalAboveItsFourLines for when such a return is refused rather than allowed to file with that residue unremoved. This fact makes that carry-forward amount visible on its own path rather than only implicit in the current-year subtraction. It is NOT itself consumed by any later-year intake this dictionary carries (no prior-year carry-IN exists either, the same gap named on /writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk), so it is disclosure, not yet a closed loop. A future unit would read this fact's value forward into a subsequent tax year's prepaid-supplies computation.

Fact.Name: Schedule F line 34 before the section 465 limitation: line 9 minus line 33, signed
Fact.Description:
Schedule F line 34, "Subtract line 33 from line 9", BEFORE any at-risk limitation. SIGNED, and deliberately not floored: a farm whose expenses exceed its gross income has a genuine loss and the printed line's own name is "Net farm profit or (loss)". Both operands are already whole dollars, so this is exact.
GATED on /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome, which is the module's ONE gate on this arm: a return that never claimed a farm resolves $0 here even if an expense writable somehow carries an amount, so no return can acquire a farm loss it did not claim. A return that DOES claim a farm and answers nothing resolves $0, which is the completeness convention /scheduleFGrossIncome set and this fact matches rather than departs from.
SUBTRACTS /scheduleFLine33 UNCHANGED, exactly as the printed instruction reads ("Subtract line 33 from line 9"): the section 464 50% prepaid farm supplies limit is now applied AT THE SOURCE, inside /scheduleFLine33's own components (/scheduleFLine16, /scheduleFLine26, /scheduleFLine28 each net the disallowed excess before this fact ever runs - see /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesDisallowed for the waterfall), so line 33 already reads the deducted total and needs no separate downstream adjustment here. Equal to the pre-section-464-unit computation on every return that does not trigger the 50% limit - the overwhelming majority.

Fact.Name: Schedule F farm loss before the at-risk limitation, as a positive amount (Form 6198 line 5)
Fact.Description: The farm's current-year loss as a POSITIVE magnitude: the absolute value of /scheduleFPreAtRiskNetProfitOrLoss when that is negative, and $0 otherwise. The input to the Form 6198 line-21 smaller-of test, which is stated in positive terms ("treat the loss on line 5 as a positive number"). Mirrors scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/rawLoss.

Fact.Name: Schedule F: section 465(a)(2) at-risk loss disallowed this year, carried to a later year (not consumed)
Fact.Description: The section 465 loss the at-risk cap disallowed this year: /scheduleFRawLoss minus /writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk, floored at $0, when the at-risk limitation applies and the loss exceeds the amount at risk - $0 otherwise (/scheduleFRawLoss itself already reflects any section 465(a)(2) carry-IN from a prior year via /scheduleFLine33's own thirty-first addend, so this figure is what a NEXT year's return should attest to, not merely this year's own loss). The Instructions for Schedule F, under "Lines 32a Through 32f," treat "any loss from this activity that wasn't allowed last year because of the at-risk rules" as a deduction allocable to the activity in the NEXT year it is filed (NOT a Form 6198 "line-34 TIP" - Form 6198 (Rev. 11-2025) has 21 lines total, none of them 34). This fact makes that amount visible on its own path rather than only implicit in the current-year cap - the same disclosure-only shape as /scheduleFPrepaidFarmSuppliesCarryForward, which named this exact gap on /writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk's own Description. The matching intake-side writable exists in THIS SAME year's dictionary (/writableScheduleFAtRiskLossFromPriorTaxYear). Each tax year's dictionary is independent, so the loop closes by FILER ATTESTATION across a year boundary, never by one year's fact reading another year's, exactly like every other ...ToNextYear/...FromPriorTaxYear pair. Mirrors scheduleC and the two scheduleE at-risk instances, which still have no carry-in intake of their own.

Fact.Name: This Schedule F's farm belongs to the secondary (MFJ spouse) filer, not the primary
Fact.Description:
Not a printed Schedule F box — an intake-only attribution question this dictionary needs because Schedule F is modelled at RETURN level (one farm's worth of facts) while Schedule SE is per-individual (IRC 1402; "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE"). True when the farm this Schedule F reports is the SECONDARY (MFJ spouse) filer's rather than the primary's. Mirrors the RETURN-LEVEL shape /scheduleCFiler carried before scheduleC.xml's own collection migration, not scheduleC's current per-item /scheduleCs/*/filer (Schedule F has no per-farm collection axis for the ordinary, non-QJV case).
ASKED ONLY WHEN RELEVANT: a return that is not MFJ, or an MFJ return with no farm at all, has no reason to see this question — the application gates the screen on /isFilingStatusMFJ AND /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome. (/isFilingStatusMFJ, not /treatAsMFJ: the block below tests the former, and a return that chose MFJ while ineligible would otherwise have a screen never shown and a block that fires.) On an MFJ return that DOES claim a farm the question is REQUIRED, not optional: leaving it blank raises /scheduleFOwnerUnansweredOnMfj, which blocks submission. OFF A JOINT RETURN THE ANSWER IS IGNORED, not obeyed: /scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler is true on every non-MFJ return whatever this fact says, because a return with one taxpayer has one Schedule SE and no spouse for a farm to belong to. A stale "yes" left behind by a filer who switched from MFJ to single or MFS therefore routes the farm back to the primary filer rather than to a chain that does not exist — the silent-correction posture scheduleC's own attribution takes, and the reason no separate secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ-style submission block is minted here. UNANSWERED DEFAULTS FALSE (the farm is the primary's) via a Placeholder, which is what keeps a single filer's return — where there is only one possible farmer — from needing the question at all, and what keeps every existing single-filer scenario at its existing attribution. The default is NOT what decides a joint return: the pairing of a primary-filer Placeholder with a mandatory submission block on the unanswered joint case is scheduleC.xml's shape for the same question about a sole proprietorship (/scheduleCs/*/filer with /scheduleCs/proprietorUnansweredOnMfj), and it exists because a silent primary default understates self-employment tax once the primary filer's own OASDI wage base is spent — or, at the other fence, lets a farm slip under his $400 line-4c threshold when it would have cleared hers. WHAT READS THE ANSWER: /scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler, and through it the two per-filer Schedule SE line 1a terms (scheduleSE:/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a and scheduleSE:/secondaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a), which route this farm's line 34 net to one spouse's Schedule SE and enter $0 on the other's.
RESIDUE, NAMED RATHER THAN CLOSED: the qualified-joint-venture case (IRC 761(f)), where BOTH spouses materially participate and elect to split the farm's items by their respective interests, needs TWO Schedule Fs and TWO Schedule SEs — a Collection this dictionary does not build. This Boolean answers "whose farm is it" for the ONE-FARM case only; a QJV election answered here would still see only one farm's income attributed whole to one spouse, never split by interest.

Fact.Name: This Schedule F's farm belongs to the primary filer
Fact.Description:
The complement of /writableScheduleFBelongsToSecondaryFiler: true unless the farm is affirmatively attributed to the secondary (MFJ spouse) filer. Unconditionally Complete, so a consumer may read it without a guard of its own.
TRUE ON EVERY RETURN THAT IS NOT MFJ, whatever the writable says. A single, HoH, QSS or MFS return has one taxpayer and one Schedule SE, so there is no second filer for a farm to belong to; an answer of "the farm is the spouse's" on such a return is ignored rather than obeyed, exactly as scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler ignores one. Without the guard the farm would route to a chain measured against a nonexistent spouse's $400 floor and OASDI base, and the printed Schedule SE would name nobody.
THE SWITCH IS LOAD-BEARING AND A BARE Not OVER THE WRITABLE IS NOT ENOUGH, which is worth stating because the shorter form reads as equivalent. The writable carries a Placeholder default, so Not over it resolves PLACEHOLDER true rather than Complete true on the unanswered return — and a Switch whose When is not Complete returns its matched case as a Placeholder, so every consumer gating on that would itself stop being Complete on the ordinary unanswered return. The same trap is why /isFilingStatusMFJ is read through an IsComplete first. The Switch tests all three, and falls through to a literal True, which is Complete.
WHAT READS IT: scheduleSE:/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a and scheduleSE:/secondaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a, the two per-filer Schedule SE line 1a terms, each of which routes /scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss to one chain and enters $0 on the other. The unanswered-on-MFJ case is not left to this fact's default: /scheduleFOwnerUnansweredOnMfj blocks submission there.

Fact.Name: The farm on this joint return does not say which spouse owns it
Fact.Description: Whether a joint return that claims Schedule F farm income never answered /writableScheduleFBelongsToSecondaryFiler. BLOCKS SUBMISSION: the farm would otherwise be filed on the primary filer's Schedule SE by that writable's default, which is an answer the filer never gave, and which understates self-employment tax whenever the primary filer's own social security wage base is already spent or the $400 line-4c threshold falls on his side of the line and not on hers. Complete FALSE on every return that claims no farm: /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome is the first conjunct and is itself complete-safe, so a joint return with no farm resolves Complete false even while /filingStatus is unanswered, and no farmless couple ever meets this block. Complete false on a return that is not joint, and false whenever the attribution is answered either way. Incomplete — and therefore blocking nothing — on a farm-claiming return whose filing status is not yet answered. COMPLETE FALSE ON AN ELECTED QUALIFIED JOINT VENTURE, whatever this attribution says or does not say. A qualified joint venture (IRC 761(f)) belongs to both spouses and is divided by their respective interests, so "which spouse owns it" has no answer to give and no default to fear; the input a QJV return cannot be allowed to leave blank is the percentage, and /scheduleFQjvInterestUnansweredOnQjv is the block that says so. The two blocks are mutually exclusive: each names the other's negation.

Fact.Name: The spouses elect qualified joint venture treatment for this farm (IRC 761(f))
Fact.Description:
Not a printed Schedule F box; an intake-only election. Question: "Do you and your spouse own and run this farm together as its only two members, does each of you materially participate in it, and are you both electing to treat it as a qualified joint venture instead of a partnership?" Help text: a farm a married couple jointly owns and operates is a partnership by default, and a partnership files Form 1065. If both spouses materially participate and both elect, the couple may instead treat it as a qualified joint venture, which "in most cases, won't increase the total tax owed on the joint return, but it does give each of you credit for social security earnings on which retirement benefits are based and for Medicare coverage without filing a partnership return" (Instructions for Schedule F, Qualified Joint Venture (QJV); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sf.pdf, page 2). All three conditions of IRC 761(f)(2) must hold: the spouses are the only members, both materially participate, and both elect.
ASKED ONLY WHEN RELEVANT: the application gates the screen on /isFilingStatusMFJ AND /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome. Section 761(f)(1) opens "In the case of a qualified joint venture conducted by a husband and wife who file a joint return for the taxable year", so a return that is not joint cannot make the election and is never asked; a return with no farm has nothing to elect over.
UNANSWERED MEANS NOT ELECTED, and that is a reading of the statute rather than a convenience: 761(f)(2)(C) requires that "both spouses elect the application of this subsection", so a return that says nothing has not elected, and the unelected treatment is what the law gives it. This is deliberately NOT the posture /writableScheduleFBelongsToSecondaryFiler takes, and the difference is worth stating. That question has no safe default, because SOME spouse owns the farm and picking one silently misstates self-employment tax, so leaving it blank blocks submission. This one does have a safe default, because "no election" is itself a complete answer the statute supplies. What has no safe default once the election IS made is the interest percentage, and that is where the submission block sits (/scheduleFQjvInterestUnansweredOnQjv). OFF A JOINT RETURN THE ANSWER IS IGNORED rather than obeyed, the same silent-correction posture /scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler takes for a stale attribution: a filer who switched from MFJ to single or MFS leaves no qualified joint venture behind, because 761(f)(1) conditions the whole subsection on a joint return. Validation: Boolean, optional. WHAT READS THE ANSWER: /scheduleFIsQualifiedJointVenture, and through it the two share facts and the two Schedule SE line 1a terms.

Fact.Name: This farm is a qualified joint venture the spouses elected (IRC 761(f))
Fact.Description:
The gate the rest of the block reads: true only when the return claims a farm, IS a joint return, and has affirmatively answered /writableScheduleFQualifiedJointVentureElection yes. Unconditionally Complete, so a consumer may read it without a guard of its own.
THREE CONJUNCTS, EACH LOAD-BEARING, and one completeness test that is easy to leave out. /claimsScheduleFFarmIncome is FIRST and is itself complete-safe, so a return with no farm resolves Complete false even while /filingStatus is unanswered. /isFilingStatusMFJ is read through an IsComplete first, because that fact is an Equal over a bare Writable with no Placeholder: on a return whose filing status is unanswered a bare Dependency would make the All Incomplete rather than Complete false, and an Incomplete When clears the Switch's accComplete and hands the fall-through arm back as a Placeholder (the same trap /scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler documents). The election writable carries NO Placeholder, so it too is read through an IsComplete before it is read at all. THE FALL-THROUGH IS A LITERAL False, which is what makes this fact Complete on every return that did not elect: the whole non-QJV corpus, and every return that is not joint. WHAT READS IT: /scheduleFQjvPrimaryFilerShare, /scheduleFQjvSecondaryFilerShare, /scheduleFQjvInterestUnansweredOnQjv, /scheduleFOwnerUnansweredOnMfj (which a QJV election MOOTS, since a qualified joint venture belongs to both spouses and the whose-farm-is-it question has no answer to give), and the two Schedule SE line 1a terms scheduleSE:/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a and scheduleSE:/secondaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's respective interest in the qualified joint venture, whole percent
Fact.Description:
Not a printed Schedule F box; the one number IRC 761(f)(1)(B) needs. Question: "What share of this farm is the primary filer's? Enter a whole percentage from 1 to 99. Your spouse's share is the rest." Help text: the statute divides "all items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit ... between the spouses in accordance with their respective interests in the venture", and the Instructions for Schedule F say the same thing in filing terms: "you must divide all items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit attributable to the farming business between you and your spouse in accordance with your respective interests in the venture" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sf.pdf, page 2). A fifty-fifty venture is entered as 50.
ASKED ONLY WHEN THE ELECTION IS MADE: the application gates the screen on /scheduleFIsQualifiedJointVenture, so no single filer and no couple that did not elect ever sees it.
UNANSWERED IS INCOMPLETE AND BLOCKS SUBMISSION, never a default, and the reason is that no default is safe. Any default hands the farm across two independent per-filer fences at once: the $176,100 OASDI wage base of IRC 1402(b)(1), which is measured against one individual's own earnings, and the $400 Schedule SE line 4c threshold, which is measured the same way. Fact.Name: The primary filer's share of Schedule F line 34 under the qualified joint venture election
Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Schedule F line 34: net farm profit or (loss)
Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Other Schedule F nonproduction receipts
Fact.Description: Actual receipts already included in Schedule F line 8 or accrual line 43 that are not from production of agricultural products or qualifying livestock, such as interest on a loan to another farmer. Enter the source receipts, not a computed conservation-income base. Fact.Name: Schedule F receipts outside the conservation-income base
Fact.Description: Custom-hire receipts, disclosed fuel and biofuel tax credits, the separately computed expense-recapture income, and identified other nonproduction receipts on the active cash or accrual form. This is subtracted only for the section 175 ceiling and never changes printed Schedule F gross income.

Fact.Name: Schedule F prior-year conservation expense carried into 2025
Fact.Description: Soil and water conservation expenditures an earlier year could not deduct because they exceeded that year section 175(b) ceiling, carried into this return against the farming business. Unanswered contributes $0. A negative answer is floored at $0 where it is read.

Fact.Name: Schedule F conservation expenditures including the prior-year carry-in
Fact.Description: This year entered conservation expenses plus the prior-year carry-in, each floored at $0 and each contributing $0 when unanswered. This is the total the section 175(b) ceiling is applied to.

Fact.Name: Schedule F conservation expense carried forward out of 2025
Fact.Description: The part of this year total, carry-in included, that the ceiling did not allow after the Form 4835 activity took its share. It leaves this return for a later year in order of time.
